records.label: The one skill that wins matches

fields.step_reason: The 4-part ritual the pros run between every point — react, release, recover, ready — so you reset your body and mind before the next ball instead of dragging the last one with you.
How to shrink the moment: turn 'I must win this' into a routine you can actually execute, so break points and set points feel like any other point.
The 4-second recovery so one mistake never becomes three. Where your eyes go, what you do with your hands, and the one sentence that lets the last point go.
Play to compete on every ball instead of playing not to lose. The mindset shift that turns your practice level into your match level when it counts.

fields.res_body: One skill underpins every other mental gain: a repeatable between-point routine. It is how the best players let go of the last ball and commit to the next. Learn the 4 steps — react, release, recover, ready — and everything else in here builds on it.
fields.res_title: The habit that separates competitors from chokers

records.label: The habit that separates competitors from chokers

fields.res_body: The score, the crowd, the last error — all of it lives in the past or the future. Your only job is the ball in front of you. A single target and a single cue word pull your attention back to now, where you can actually play.

You cannot stop thoughts — but you do not have to obey them. Name the thought ('I'm rushing'), take one breath, return to your cue word. The thought fades on its own when you stop fighting it and go back to the routine.

A racing heart before a match is not fear — it is your body getting ready to compete. Call it 'ready', not 'nervous'. Same feeling, different meaning. Breathe slow on the exhale and let that energy sharpen your first move instead of shrinking it.

Break points feel huge because you make them huge. Turn 'I must win this' into the exact routine you run on every point — bounce, breathe, target, commit. When the big point is just another rep of your routine, the pressure has nowhere to grab.

Confidence is not a feeling you wait for — it is a decision to play your patterns. Name the two shots you trust most and build every point around them. When in doubt, go to your strength; it is the fastest way back to belief.

Your body leads your mind, not the other way around. Walk tall between points, head up, racket up, shoulders back — even when you're behind. The posture of a confident player changes how you feel and how your opponent reads you.

One error becomes three when you drag it with you. Turn to the back fence, one long exhale, unclench your hand, drop your shoulders. Four seconds. The point is gone — the only ball that matters is the next one.

Sit, towel, five slow breaths. Ask one question: what is working, and what is my ONE adjustment this game? Leave the scoreboard alone. Stand up with a single clear intention — a fresh story for the next games.
